content:
Earlier this week, a report indicated that some iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users experienced their devices freezing and rebooting after failed Face ID authentication. At the time, we believed the issue was a software bug rather than a hardware fault.

Apple has confirmed to 9to5Mac that it will release a software update to address the issue, which is expected to be available early next week.

Although the bug does not affect all users, affected instances appear to be fairly widespread based on social media and reports from 9to5Mac readers.

We were able to reproduce the issue on an iPhone 18 Pro by covering the screen with a palm and attempting to log in to the Passwords app via Face ID. The device completely stopped responding to touch input and force-restarted after several seconds. Users can then find the relevant panic log in the Analytics section of the Settings app.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max feature a redesigned Face ID sensor system, with the infrared camera relocated beneath the display near the status bar clock, reducing the visible Dynamic Island area by 25%.

As we reported earlier this week, some customers mistook the issue for a hardware fault and attempted to get their devices replaced by Apple to resolve the rebooting problem. To reiterate, it has now been confirmed that the issue will be fixed via a software update, and there is no need to seek a replacement.

On a related note, Apple has also just released watchOS 27.0.1 to address random rebooting issues affecting the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
